reading: The same definition, a reading: Unified Billing lets merchants buy apps through the BigCommerce App Marketplace and have the charges included on their BigCommerce invoice (BC-S-0172, BC-S-0183), as Shopify adds app charges to the merchant's Shopify invoice (SH-S-0281) and Salla takes a paid app's payment through its platform (SA-S-0025). Strained: no BigCommerce statement says Commerce keeps a share; its statements make Commerce the Unified Billing Partners' collection agent (BC-S-0175, BC-S-0179), and the disbursement to partners is also cited in CM-PTN-003 and the Partner Portal account condition (BC-S-0174) in CM-PTN-002, the PTN tree, and the Unified Billing API's account-level tokens (BC-S-0181) in CM-API-013, the API tree.

Joined by the term Admin API, a reading: BigCommerce's Admin API, GraphQL ("Query and mutate store data server-side", BC-S-0296; Admin API [graphql], BC-I-0110), and Shopify's GraphQL Admin API (SH-I-0044) are each platform's API for reading and writing a store's data.

A new capability: the GraphQL Account API manages account-level resources such as control panel users (BC-S-0298, BC-S-0299), and account-level credentials reach all the account's stores (BC-S-0301). No capability of the model so far is an API over the account rather than a store. Its statements are cited only here; the Unified Billing API's use of account-level tokens (BC-S-0181, a statement of BC-C-029) is cited here too.

Joined by the term OAuth, a reading: BigCommerce's OAuth-based API accounts, store-level, app-level and account-level credentials (BC-S-0302), and their OAuth scope (BC-S-0307), as Salla supports OAuth 2.0 for authorization (SA-S-0176) and Shopify lists API authentication (SH-I-0030). Its scopes are cited in CM-API-003 and its user-information term in CM-API-004, both in the API-001 tree. Strained: the store-level API accounts a merchant creates in Settings > Store-level API accounts (BC-S-0303) are cited in CM-APP-009, the APP tree.

Joined by the term rate limit, a reading: apps using OAuth are rate-limited on a quota refreshed every 30 seconds, varying by store plan (BC-S-0308, BC-S-0312), with rate limits as safeguards for reliability (BC-S-0316), as Salla's Rate Limiting (SA-S-1001) and Shopify's Limits (SH-I-0036).

Joined by the term Webhooks, a reading: BigCommerce's Webhooks v3 (BC-I-0076), "Get notified when specific events occur on a BigCommerce store" (BC-S-0317), as Shopify's Webhooks (SH-I-0027) and Salla's (SA-S-1008).

Joined by the term apps, a reading: BigCommerce's two types of apps, single-click and connector (BC-S-0324), and its App Marketplace (BC-S-0325), as Shopify's Apps (SH-S-1495) and Salla's My apps (SA-S-1883). It holds apps and the marketplace together, so it lands in the parent, coarser than CM-APP-002; its marketplace statements are cited there, its uninstall topic in CM-APP-004, its unlisted apps in CM-APP-009, all in the APP-001 tree. Strained: the app types are defined by the method of authentication, and BC-S-0324 and the single-click access token (BC-S-0330) are also cited in CM-API-002, the API tree; its Ecommerce AI category (BC-I-0477) is cited in CM-AIA-001.

Joined on role, a reading: BigCommerce's MCP server connects AI agents to storefronts to search products, manage carts and hand off to checkout (BC-S-0342), and its Agentic checkout enables transactions within AI-powered shopping experiences while the merchant remains merchant of record (BC-S-0347); Shopify's developers build commerce agents acting for buyers with its UCP-compliant MCP servers (SH-S-0714) and WebMCP Tools (SH-I-0073). Not CM-AIA-004: there the MCP server links the merchant's assistant to the store; here it serves AI agents shopping the storefront (notes.md).

Joined by the term AI features, a reading: BigCommerce's AI Features (BC-S-0351; the AI Features Addendum, BC-I-0473) and Shopify's AI features in the Shopify admin (SH-S-7488). It lands in the parent: its BigCommerce Companion (BC-S-0349) is cited in CM-AIA-002 and its BigAI (BC-S-0350) in CM-AIA-003, both children of CM-AIA-001.

A new capability: Powered By is a collection of partner-focused APIs that let a partner offer BigCommerce stores to its merchants and onboard them (BC-S-0361), with an API group of its own, Beta Powered By > Stores and > Plans (BC-S-0359, BC-S-0363), and the partner may own the billing relationship (BC-S-0362). No capability of the model so far is a platform reselling its stores through partners.

A new capability: Staging environments, to test, preview and deploy updates without disrupting live storefronts (BC-S-0413), with StagingPro, a sandbox, testing, staging and CI/CD solution for Enterprise-level stores (BC-S-0414). No capability of the model so far stages a store's changes; development stores (CM-DVT-004) are free stores for building apps and themes.

Joined on role, a reading: BigCommerce's Third-Party Products, which Commerce may disable at any time (BC-S-0462) and whose dealings are solely between the merchant and the provider (BC-S-0463), have the role of Shopify's Third Party Services, which Shopify may disable at any time (SH-S-0060) and whose use is solely between the merchant and the provider (SH-S-0058), and of WooCommerce's Third-Party Services (WC-S-0487). The terms differ (Products, Services), the role is the same. Its Extension statement (BC-S-0464) is cited in CM-APP-011, in the APP-001 tree.

Joined on role, a reading: the Merchant-Client Terms (BC-I-0465) apply when someone uses the Services on behalf of a third-party client, as its agent (BC-S-0474), and must confirm that relationship to Commerce in writing (BC-S-0477); the partner programme's terms bind those who work with merchants on Shopify (SH-S-0288) and Salla (SA-S-0213). Strained: no BigCommerce statement names a partner programme for these agents; the terms bind anyone acting for a client. It lands in the parent because no child fits, and the Merchant-Client Terms are a legal agreement, not an admin section, API group, plan line or app category, so it makes no capability of its own.
